source_book: NCERT Class 11 Physics Ch.6 Work, Energy and Power — table-of-contents scope only (the concept of potential energy sits between the conservative/non-conservative material and energy conservation), teaching authored from first principles. The atomic concept: potential energy U is energy stored by POSITION against a conservative force, DEFINED by ΔU = −W_conservative — when gravity does −40 J of work, the stored energy rises by exactly +40 J: the same size change, the opposite sign, in the same frames — and only a conservative force can have a U at all, because only its work is a single number per position (friction's is not, so 'friction potential energy' does not exist). Does NOT teach U = mgh or any formula for U's value, the freedom to choose the h = 0 reference, or path independence (all gravitational_potential_energy, #7 — the dashed U = 0 line at the ramp's foot is named once as 'where the count starts' and never discussed as a choice); does NOT teach spring PE (#8 — no spring); does NOT do K, E_total or conservation (#9 — no K bar anywhere); does NOT do the accounting of where friction's heat goes (#10 — S2 names the destination in one authored clause, nothing more); and does NOT re-teach the work meter (work_done_by_constant_force, #1), work's sign (positive_negative_zero_work, #2) or the round-trip test (conservative_vs_nonconservative_forces, #5 — consumed in one leaning clause, never re-run). Built on the newtons_laws_body field_3d engine with the SEAM K/L/M/N energy layer — the first concept in the fleet to render the U_grav energy bar, the first to pair the energy layer with a work accumulator where the claim IS their numeric CHANGE-identity (ΔU = −W_c), and the first to author capture_mode 'first' with dwell_ms. STATE_3 teaches from two labelled points A and B (marker 'point', the SEAM-M teaching dwell): the scene HOLDS 2 s at each stamped crossing so a teacher can read U and gravity's work together before the motion resumes. STATE_1/STATE_2 deliberately carry their claims on the live bars alone — their truths are continuous, a lock-step mirror at every frame — so the point instrument appears exactly where the claim is a difference between two places.

real_world_anchor.primary: A pumped-storage hydroelectric plant. At night, spare electricity pumps water uphill into a high reservoir; at peak hours the water runs back down through the turbines. A whole power grid stores energy by position — and the energy it gets back is exactly minus the work gravity did while the water was pumped up.
real_world_anchor.secondary: A rooftop water tank. A pump pushes water up to a tank above a building; open a tap and the stored energy comes back — the water flows down on its own.

h_ref.name: energy reference height (the U = 0 line, measured from the ramp's foot)

s0.name: home position along the track (+s is up-slope)

F_grav_parallel.name: gravity's component along the incline (always down-slope)

constraints: Delta-U = -W_gravity at every instant, for any motion, rough or smooth, guided or dragged — the definitional law this concept teaches
U = m * g * (s * sin(theta) - h_ref) is a pure function of position s only, never of time or velocity directly
friction's work is path-dependent (proportional to cumulative |ds| since s_ref, not to net displacement), so friction has no potential energy
U >= 0 everywhere on the track for h_ref = -3.05 m; the guard margin is >= 1.96 J at the track's lowest reachable point (s = -6 m)
h_ref = -3.05 m is IDENTICAL in all four states -- the U = 0 reference never moves at any state transition
normal force N = m * g * cos(theta) is constant -- the block never leaves the incline surface in any state

aha_moment.statement: Gravity's negative work is not lost — U rises by the same joules, opposite sign.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The block climbs a frictionless slope: as gravity's work bar falls to −128.0 J, the U bar climbs from 49.0 to 177.0 J — equal joule changes, opposite directions, in the same frames.

scene_composition.text: a 4 kg block is launched up a frictionless 30° slope at 8 m/s, starting 1.25 m above the dashed U = 0 line at the ramp's foot

the U bar opens at 49.0 J and climbs to 177.0 J at the 1.63 s apex while gravity's work bar falls to −128.0 J — equal joule changes, opposite directions, every frame; on the descent both bars mirror back
the HUD's v row tracks speed, and the formula surface reads ΔU = −W gravity

tts_sentences.text_en: Like a pumped-storage plant, this block stores energy by position.
U, the potential energy, counts from the dashed line at the ramp's foot, opening at 49.0 joules.
Going up, gravity's work falls to negative 128 joules while U climbs equally.
Coming down, gravity's work turns positive, climbing back toward zero as U falls back equally.

misconception_watch.belief: Negative work means the energy is gone
misconception_watch.visual_counter: As gravity's bar falls from 0 to −128.0 J, the U bar climbs from 49.0 to 177.0 J — up by the same 128.0 J in the same frames; on the descent U falls back exactly as gravity's total climbs back toward zero
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Gravity's negative work is stored as potential energy and returned on the way down — moved, not destroyed

scene_composition.text: same 30° slope now rough (μₛ = μₖ = 0.35), same 8 m/s launch — only friction is new
a third bar joins: friction falls to −48.3 J at the 1.02 s apex and keeps falling to −91.2 J by the loop's end, on both legs, while U still climbs and falls joule-for-joule with gravity's bar
the HUD reads v and f = 11.9 N, and the formula surface reads ΔU = −W conservative

tts_sentences.text_en: Same rough slope, same launch speed.
A third bar joins: friction, falling going up, and falling coming down.
No partner rises to meet it.
U keeps its joule-for-joule lock with gravity's work, both ways.
Friction's joules become heat, a later lesson tracks them.
Only conservative forces have a potential energy.

misconception_watch.belief: Work done against any force is stored, friction too
misconception_watch.visual_counter: On the rough trip U still moves joule-for-joule with gravity's bar, while friction's bar falls on both legs and no bar rises to meet it — friction's joules become heat, not into any stored-by-position number
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Friction's work depends on the path taken, not the position reached, so no single stored number per position can exist for it — only conservative forces have a potential energy

STATE_3.title: Only the change in U matches

scene_composition.text: a slower 7 m/s launch, frictionless — the block crosses two marked points, A then B, along the slope

the scene freezes 2 s at each crossing: point A stamps U = 88.2 J, W gravity = −39.2 J; point B stamps U = 135.2 J, W gravity = −86.2 J — the levels differ, but 135.2 − 88.2 = 47.0 J is exactly minus the work gravity did between them
the HUD reads v, and the formula surface reads ΔU = −W gravity (A → B)

tts_sentences.text_en: The block crosses point A, then point B, the scene freezes.
The levels don't match, but the change does: U rose by 47.0 joules, and gravity's work fell equally.
The next concept gives gravity's U its own formula, and lets you place the U = 0 line wherever you like.

scene_composition.text: the sandbox opens MOVING — the same 8 m/s launch as STATE_1, both friction dials at zero — with the same dashed U = 0 line and the same 49.0 J opening
drag the block anywhere on the slope, raise either friction dial, or relaunch at any speed — the U bar and both work ledgers re-derive live, and ΔU = −W gravity holds through every motion
three live dials: launch speed v₀ (0–8 m/s), static friction μₛ and kinetic friction μₖ (both 0–0.5, capped below tan 30° so no corner sticks)

tts_sentences.text_en: Drag the block anywhere on the slope.
U always tracks its height above the dashed line.
Raise friction, and its bar falls both ways with no partner.
Relaunch faster — U at the same height never changes.

regeneration_variants.label: A Skateboarder Launched Up a Ramp
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A skateboarder rides up a smooth ramp at speed, coasts to the top, and rolls back down. A second run adds a rough patch that only removes speed, never returns it.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical readings: the same U bar and gravity work bar move by equal joules in opposite directions on the smooth run; on the rough run a third bar falls on both legs with no partner rising to meet it.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same single-body rig, same inclined track — only the block becomes a skater.

regeneration_variants.label: A Mine Cart Rolling on a Hillside Track
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A mine cart is released up a sloped rail track, climbs, and rolls back down under gravity alone; a second run adds a rough rail section.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Same law, same numbers: the cart's U bar and gravity's work ledger always move by equal joules, opposite signs, every frame; a rough section adds a third bar that never gets a partner.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same rig and physics — the block is relabelled a cart, the slope becomes a rail track.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student who has mastered this concept can state the definition ΔU = −W_conservative; explain why a force must be conservative (path-independent) to have a potential energy at all; predict the sign of ΔU from the sign of a conservative force's work, in either direction of motion; compute ΔU between two marked points from the work done between them, without needing an absolute reference; and explain that U depends only on position, never on speed.

questions.stem: A ball is launched up a frictionless slope. While it climbs, is the work done by gravity positive or negative? What happens to the potential energy U during the climb?

options.A: Gravity's work is negative; U rises by exactly the same amount gravity's work falls.
options.B: Gravity's work is negative; U falls by the same amount gravity's work falls.
options.C: Gravity's work is positive; U rises as the ball climbs.
options.D: Gravity's work is negative; U cannot be found without knowing the ball's speed.

distractor_misconceptions.B: confuses the sign of gravity's work with the sign of the change in U — the definition makes them opposite, not equal
distractor_misconceptions.C: reverses gravity's own sign convention: gravity always points down-slope, so its work while climbing is negative, not positive
distractor_misconceptions.D: treats U as dependent on speed — U is a pure function of position only, never of velocity

questions.tested_idea: negative work by gravity produces an equal, positive change in U — the definition's sign, qualitative case
questions.parallel_form_stem: A cart is pushed up a frictionless ramp. While it climbs, is the work done by gravity positive or negative, and what happens to U?

questions.stem: As the block moves from its highest point back down the slope, is the work done by gravity on that leg positive or negative? Does U rise or fall over that same leg?

options.A: Gravity's work is positive; U falls by the same amount.
options.B: Gravity's work is negative; U falls.
options.C: Gravity's work is positive; U also rises.
options.D: Gravity's work is positive; U stays the same, since the block already reached its highest point.

distractor_misconceptions.B: mistakes gravity's sign as a fixed property of the force instead of one set by the direction of motion relative to the force — on the descent gravity acts with the motion, so its work is positive
distractor_misconceptions.C: assumes work and the change in U always move the same way — the definition makes them opposite in sign at every instant, ascent or descent
distractor_misconceptions.D: treats U as fixed once the highest point is reached, missing that U keeps changing as the block keeps moving

questions.tested_idea: gravity's work sign is set by the direction of motion relative to the force, not a fixed property of the force
questions.parallel_form_stem: As a cart rolls back down a frictionless ramp from its highest point, is gravity's work on that leg positive or negative, and does U rise or fall?

questions.stem: A block is dragged across a rough floor and back to its start. Explain why there is no 'potential energy of friction,' and state where the energy removed by friction actually goes.

options.A: Friction's work depends on the path taken, not the position reached, so no single number-per-position exists for it — the energy becomes heat.
options.B: Friction's work is destroyed — it disappears completely once the block stops.
options.C: Friction does have a potential energy, just like gravity, since its work can also be computed with a formula.
options.D: Friction's energy is stored in the block's motion and is released the next time the block moves.

distractor_misconceptions.B: the belief this concept exists to correct — negative work is never destroyed, it becomes heat, not nothing
distractor_misconceptions.C: mistakes computability of work for storability — friction's work CAN be calculated, but only a path-independent force gives a single value per position
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses heat with kinetic energy — friction's dissipated joules become heat in the block and floor, not stored motion energy released later

questions.tested_idea: only path-independent (conservative) forces can have a potential energy — friction fails the round-trip test
questions.parallel_form_stem: A crate is pushed across a rough table and back to its start. Explain why there is no 'potential energy of friction,' and state where the removed energy goes.

questions.stem: Between two marked points on a slope, gravity does −50 J of work on a block. What is the change in the block's potential energy between those two points?

options.C: U at the second point equals −50 J
options.D: ΔU cannot be found without knowing the reference height

distractor_misconceptions.B: drops the minus sign in the definition ΔU = −W — the change in U is the negative of the work done
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses the CHANGE in U with the LEVEL of U at a point — exactly the distinction this state's stamps exist to teach; the level needs a reference, the change does not
distractor_misconceptions.D: the definition ΔU = −W needs no reference height at all — only the LEVEL of U needs one, not the change

questions.tested_idea: ΔU = −W_gravity gives the CHANGE directly from the work done, with no reference needed
questions.parallel_form_stem: Between two marked points on a slope, gravity does +30 J of work on a block. What is the change in the block's potential energy between those two points?

questions.stem: State the general definition of potential energy in terms of work, and explain why this definition can only apply to certain forces.

options.A: ΔU = −W_conservative; only forces whose work is path-independent can have a potential energy defined this way.
options.B: ΔU = −W for any force whose work can be calculated with a formula.
options.C: ΔU = −W_conservative, and every force in mechanics qualifies, since work can always be computed.
options.D: U = −W_conservative, so U itself, not just its change, equals minus the work done.

distractor_misconceptions.B: mistakes computability of work for storability — any force's work can be calculated, but only a path-independent one gives a single value per position
distractor_misconceptions.C: the exact scope error the definition exists to prevent — friction's work IS computable, yet friction has no U, because its work is path-dependent
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses the LEVEL U with the CHANGE ΔU — the definition constrains the change, not an absolute value of U itself

questions.tested_idea: the definition ΔU = −W_conservative and why it is undefined for a path-dependent force
questions.parallel_form_stem: State the general definition of potential energy in terms of work, and name one force it cannot apply to, with a reason.

questions.stem: A block is released from the same height on a frictionless slope twice — once launched slowly, once launched fast. Compare the potential energy U at that height in the two cases.

options.A: U is identical in both cases — it depends only on position, never on speed.
options.B: The faster block has more potential energy, since it has more total energy.
options.C: The slower block has more potential energy, since it spends more time at that height.
options.D: U cannot be compared without also knowing each block's kinetic energy.

distractor_misconceptions.B: confuses kinetic energy, which does depend on speed, with potential energy, which does not — U is a pure function of position only
distractor_misconceptions.C: invents a time-dependence for U that does not exist — U depends only on where the block is, not how long it stays there
distractor_misconceptions.D: assumes U needs K to be meaningful — U at a position is fully determined by that position alone

questions.tested_idea: U depends only on position, never on speed — a transfer check separating U from kinetic energy
questions.parallel_form_stem: A cart passes through the same height on a frictionless ramp on two different runs, once slow and once fast. Compare its potential energy U at that height in the two runs.

STATE_1.label: A 4 kg block is launched up a frictionless 30° slope at 8 m/s from 1.25 m above the dashed U = 0 line at the ramp's foot; over 1.63 s to the apex the U bar climbs from 49.0 to 177.0 J while gravity's work bar falls from 0.0 to −128.0 J — equal joule changes, opposite directions, every frame; on the descent gravity's work climbs back toward zero as U falls back by the same joules; the loop resets at 3150 ms.
STATE_1.caption: Negative work, stored as U

STATE_2.label: Same 30° slope, now rough (μₛ = μₖ = 0.35), same 8 m/s launch: a third bar joins — friction — falling to −48.3 J at the 1.02 s apex and continuing to fall to −91.2 J by the 2.95 s loop end, on both legs; U still climbs and falls joule-for-joule with gravity's bar throughout.
STATE_2.caption: No store for friction

STATE_3.label: A slower 7 m/s launch, frictionless: the block crosses point A (s = −1.6 m) at 322 ms, where the scene freezes 2 s and stamps 'point A: U = 88.2 J · W gravity = −39.2 J'; it then crosses point B (s = +0.8 m) and freezes again, stamping 'point B: U = 135.2 J · W gravity = −86.2 J' — the levels differ, but 135.2 − 88.2 = 47.0 J is exactly minus the work gravity did between them; the loop resets at 6600 ms.
STATE_3.caption: ΔU equals −W gravity

STATE_4.label: Sandbox: the block opens moving — the same 8 m/s launch as STATE_1, both friction dials at zero — with the same dashed U = 0 line and the same 49.0 J opening; drag the block, raise either friction dial (capped below tan 30° so no corner sticks), or relaunch at any speed, and ΔU = −W gravity holds through every motion.
STATE_4.caption: Change anything
